title: Magnets
examples: What kind of things can magnets pull towards them?
How do magnets push things away?
Where are the strong parts of a magnet?

explain.say: A magnet can pull some things towards it. This pulling is called attraction.
Now look! Here it is in 3D: a bar magnet. Can you see the north pole and the south pole? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.
Some magnets will push things away from them. This pushing is called repulsion.
Every magnet has two ends called poles. These poles are called North and South.
The North pole and the South pole of two magnets always pull together. This is attraction.

draw.text: N pole to S pole: Attract

explain.say: If you try to push two North poles together, they will push apart. This is repulsion.

draw.text: N pole to N pole: Repel

explain.say: Magnets only stick to certain materials, like iron. They do not stick to wood or plastic.

faq.q: What materials do magnets like to stick to?
faq.a: Magnets are strongest with certain metals like iron and steel. They do not stick to things like plastic or wood.
asks: What can a magnet pick up?

faq.q: Why do magnets push each other away sometimes?
faq.a: Magnets push away when the poles are the same. North pushing North, or South pushing South, will repel.

faq.q: Do magnets have a beginning and an end?
faq.a: Yes, every magnet has two ends called poles. These are always a North pole and a South pole.
asks: What are the ends of a magnet called?
How many poles does a magnet have?

faq.q: Does the magnet have to be big to work?
faq.a: No, even a small magnet can show attraction or repulsion. The poles are what matters most.
asks: Can a small magnet do this?

faq.q: If I mix magnets, what happens?
faq.a: If you put a North pole near a South pole, they will attract. If you put two North poles together, they will repel.
asks: How do I make them stick?

facts: Magnets have two poles: North and South.
Magnets are attracted to magnetic materials like iron.

quiz.say: If you put a North pole near a South pole, what happens?
quiz.why: Opposite poles, North and South, always pull together.

wrong.1: This is wrong because North and South poles are opposites.
wrong.2: This is wrong because magnets always show a force.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the result is attraction, not just a type of attraction.

quiz.say: Which material will a magnet most likely stick to?
quiz.why: Iron is a common magnetic material that magnets are known to attract.

wrong.0: Rubber is not magnetic, so the magnet will not stick to it.
wrong.2: Wood is not a magnetic material, so the magnet will not stick.
wrong.3: Plastic is not magnetic, so the magnet will not pull it.

quiz.say: If I try to push two South poles together, what force do I feel?
quiz.why: Like poles, South and South, push each other apart, which is repulsion.

wrong.0: This is wrong because like poles push away from each other.
wrong.1: This is wrong because magnets always show a force.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the force is pushing, not pulling.
